steps.name: Hallmark GSEA preranked from DESeq2 results
caveats: de_results.csv gene symbols may not all match HGNC symbols used in the Hallmark GMT (case, aliases, version suffixes) — report the match/miss rate rather than silently dropping unmatched genes without comment
GSEA prerank results depend on permutation count and seed; use a reasonable permutation number (e.g. 1000) for stable p-values given only 50 gene sets, and fix the seed for reproducibility
Do not conflate nominal p-value with FDR q-value when reporting 'significant' pathways
This is enrichment on a pre-computed DE contrast, not a re-derivation of differential expression — do not recompute or second-guess the DESeq2 results themselves in this step
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are significantly enriched (positively or negatively) in the atopic dermatitis lesional vs control contrast, based on the existing DESeq2 log2_fold_change / p-value results for all ~12000 genes?
constraints: Use Python only, per explicit user constraint — no R packages or scripts
Use the existing de_results.csv as the sole source of gene-level statistics; do not recompute DESeq2 from counts.csv
Use the MSigDB human Hallmark GMT from the reference store; do not substitute GO or oncogenic collections for this question
acceptance_criteria: Loads de_results.csv (12000 genes) and confirms columns gene, log2_fold_change, and a p-value column are present and usable

Builds a signed ranking metric (sign(log2_fold_change) * -log10(pvalue)); genes with missing/zero p-values or NA log2FC are handled explicitly (dropped or imputed with justification) and the count dropped is reported
Deduplicates any repeated gene symbols before building the ranked list (report how many collapsed and how, e.g. by max abs stat)
Loads the 50 MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (HALLMARK_* symbol GMT) from the reference store and reports how many of the ranked genes map into at least one hallmark set (match rate)
Runs gseapy prerank (or equivalent preranked GSEA) with a fixed random seed and reports NES, p-value, and FDR q-value for all 50 hallmark terms
Produces a results table (all 50 terms, sorted by NES or FDR) and a plot (e.g., barplot or dotplot of top enriched terms in each direction) saved to the step's output directory
Explicitly flags terms significant at FDR < 0.25 (standard GSEA threshold) and separately at FDR < 0.05, without claiming significance where it was not met

plan.title: AD lesional vs control hallmark GSEA enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset already provides a DESeq2 results table (12000 x 8: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, ...) for the AD lesional vs control contrast (6 vs 6, unpaired). The research question only asks which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched in this contrast, so no re-computation of differential expression is needed — the analysis starts directly from de_results.csv. The plan has a single analytical step: rank all genes by a signed statistic (sign(log2FC) * -log10(p-value), falling back to log2FC alone if a stat column is unusable) and run pre-ranked GSEA (gseapy prerank, Python only per user constraint) against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets staged in the reference store. Output is a ranked, FDR-annotated table of enriched Hallmark pathways plus a summary plot, with explicit reporting of gene-symbol match rate against the hallmark gene universe (Salmon gene-symbol counts can have version suffixes or synonyms that fail to map) and of any duplicate gene rows collapsed before ranking.
